hypotheses.justification: The statement is still true when p is not prime. In that case `Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_prime` gives `m.factorization p = 0` and `n.factorization p = 0`. So `ordCompl[p] m = m / p^0 = m`, `ordCompl[p] n = n`, and `min 0 0 = 0`. The right side becomes `gcd m n * p^0 = gcd m n`, which is the left side. This covers p = 0 and p = 1 as well. The proof splits with `by_cases hp : p.Prime`. The prime case is the existing proof. The non-prime case is `simp [Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_prime _ hp]`. The other two hypotheses cannot be dropped, because for prime p, m = 0 and n = p make the statement false (left side p, right side 1). The symmetric case, n = 0 and m = p, fails the same way.
